questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to verify the delivery timeline and decide if you need to switch to a faster payment method or a different app before committing to the transfer.
questions.check: Does the review screen state whether funds arrive in minutes or take several business days?
questions.say_example: This says funds arrive <in minutes/in 1-3 business days>

questions.question: Does the registered banking name match the person you intend to pay?
questions.why: The review screen displays the recipient's actual enrolled banking name (e.g., 'Enrolled as [name]'), which is your only safeguard to catch if their phone number or email was reassigned to a stranger.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the critical security check of verifying the recipient's true registered bank name, risking an irreversible transfer to a stranger who inherited your contact's old phone number.
questions.check: Does the registered/enrolled name shown on the review screen match the person you were told you're paying?
questions.say_example: This is enrolled as <a different name> than the one you told me. Those don't match.

children.label: Check the fees and exchange rate

questions.question: Are the sending and receiving amounts correct based on the shown conversion rate?
questions.why: The screen displays a dynamic currency conversion rate from MXN to USD that includes a fee, making it important to verify the amounts before proceeding.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to evaluate whether the exchange rate is acceptable and to personalize the payment note for the recipient.
questions.verify_form: Check the conversion pair against the shown rate, then read the note the agent typed; the arithmetic is on screen, the note text is its invention.
questions.check: Do the sending and receiving amounts shown match what the displayed exchange rate and fee should produce?
questions.say_example: At this rate and fee, sending <$100> should show <€92> received. The screen shows <€85> instead.

questions.question: What exactly are the fees and exchange rates applied to this transfer?
questions.why: Inspecting the payment breakdown and fee modal ensures you understand the exact costs, including the exchange rate and the £0.18 international fee, before sending the money.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally scrutinize the itemized fees and exchange rate to ensure the transaction costs are acceptable.
questions.check: Does the fee modal show the exchange rate and the flat fee applied to this transfer?
questions.say_example: The rate here is <1.08>, plus a <$2.50> fee.

questions.question: The rate isn't locked in yet, so the final amount could still change. Is that OK?
questions.why: The screen warns that the displayed conversion rate includes a fee and that the final amount you pay may fluctuate until the rate is officially locked in.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to acknowledge the risk of currency fluctuation and decide whether to proceed with an estimated cost rather than a fixed one.
questions.verify_form: The rate warning means the debited amount can move between review and settlement - check the final receipt's rate against the review's; accepting that drift happened at the agent's Send.
questions.check: Does the final settled amount shown at completion or on the receipt match the amount shown at review time?
questions.say_example: Review showed <$80>, but the receipt shows <$76>. The rate moved after you sent.

questions.question: Is there a scam warning on this screen before you can send?
questions.why: The screen displays a prominent scam alert and various account options like Zelle preferences that might affect how you safely send money.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to read the platform's current security warnings and proactively adjust your account preferences before making a transaction.
questions.verify_form: A scam alert and the preference menus sat on the landing screen - check whether the agent read past them straight to Send; the warning names exactly the failure this payment can have.
questions.check: Does the landing screen display a scam or fraud warning before the Send button?
questions.say_example: There's a scam warning on this screen. I'm reading it before going further.

questions.question: Before you check this box: is this really the person you're paying?
questions.why: The app requires you to verify the recipient's identity and acknowledge a fraud warning by checking a box before you can proceed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally verify the recipient's identity and evaluate the fraud warnings before the money is sent.
questions.verify_form: A checkbox swore this is really the person you mean - check who was on that screen when the agent ticked it; the box exists because this payment cannot be pulled back.
questions.check: Does the screen require checking a box confirming the recipient's identity and acknowledging a fraud warning before continuing?
questions.say_example: Before this checkbox, is <name> really who you're paying? There's no undo after this.

questions.question: After checking the scam-warning box, does tapping Continue come next?
questions.why: The screen requires you to explicitly acknowledge the fraud warning by checking a box and tapping Continue before the payment can proceed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the intended moment of friction where you would personally evaluate the risk of fraud before releasing your funds.
questions.check: Does the screen require tapping Continue after the scam-warning box is checked?
questions.say_example: Tapped Continue past the scam-warning box

questions.question: Are you sure? Once this sends, it can't be cancelled.
questions.why: The screen explicitly warns that the payment cannot be cancelled once sent, making this the final chance to back out.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the final opportunity to personally verify the recipient's identity and stop an irreversible transfer of funds.
questions.verify_form: The no-cancel popup is the gate that matters - check what was on screen when the agent tapped Yes: recipient and amount, because there is no undo after it.
questions.check: Does the screen state this payment cannot be cancelled once sent?
questions.say_example: This is the last screen. Once sent, it can't be cancelled. Send it?

questions.question: Does the funding source and balance shown here match what you saw earlier?
questions.why: The available balance shown earlier should be correctly applied or reflected on the final payment authorization screen to avoid unexpected charges to a backup payment method.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to ensure their available app balance is correctly utilized instead of an external card.
questions.check: Does the funding source and balance shown on the authorization screen match what was shown earlier?
questions.say_example: Balance shown here is <$120>, but it read <$140> earlier

questions.question: Is the bank asking for an extra security code before this can go through?
questions.why: If the transaction is unusually large or to a new recipient, the app or linked bank may interrupt the review screen with a mandatory step-up security challenge to prevent fraud.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to intercept the OTP sent to their phone or realize that their bank considers this specific transaction high-risk.
questions.check: Does the app or bank interrupt with an extra security-code step before finalizing?
questions.say_example: The bank wants a one-time code before this can finish

questions.question: Is the app asking for the UPI PIN of the linked account before the money moves?
questions.why: The screen indicates that you must enter your existing UPI PIN for the account ending in [last4] to complete the payment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step requires sharing a highly sensitive personal PIN with an agent, which compromises the security of the linked bank account.
questions.check: Does the screen ask for the UPI PIN of the linked account before completing the payment?
questions.say_example: Entered the UPI PIN to complete the payment

questions.question: What do you do if the SMS security code fails to arrive?
questions.why: The verification screen includes a countdown timer to 'Resend code', which is your only recourse if the network silently fails to deliver the required SMS to authorize the payment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to monitor the delivery of the security code and manually trigger a retry, potentially leaving the transaction permanently stalled.
questions.check: Does the screen show a countdown with a Resend option for a security code that hasn't arrived?
questions.say_example: The code hasn't arrived yet. There's a Resend option once the countdown ends.

children.label: Verify the outcome
children.note: 8.1 then 8.2 and 8.3 - the balance moves before the history shows it; 8.4 through 8.6 where offered

questions.question: Did the payment go through, to the right person, for the right amount?
questions.why: Checking the 'Money Sent' summary confirms that the transaction was processed exactly as intended.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the immediate peace of mind of seeing the final confirmation screen to verify the money went to the right place.
questions.check: Does the confirmation screen show the payment as sent, with the correct amount and recipient?
questions.say_example: Sent. <$27> went to <recipient>.

questions.question: Is the payment only initiated, and still waiting for the recipient to accept it?
questions.why: The confirmation bubble with 'Remind' and 'Cancel' buttons confirms the transfer was initiated but is still waiting for the recipient to accept it.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the direct visual confirmation that the money was sent and the awareness that the recipient still needs to actively accept the funds.
questions.check: Does the confirmation show Remind and Cancel buttons, meaning the transfer is initiated but waiting on the recipient to accept?
questions.say_example: This is sent but still pending. <recipient> needs to accept it.

questions.question: Did the app display a network error or timeout after you tapped send?
questions.why: If the app loses connection during processing, it is unclear if the payment actually went through, creating a high risk of double-paying if you blindly retry.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the critical context needed to decide whether to check your bank statement first or immediately attempt the payment again.
questions.check: Did the app show a network error or timeout right after Send was tapped?
questions.say_example: A network error showed right after sending. I'm checking whether it went through before trying again. Sending twice would be a second, separate payment.

questions.question: Did a quick success animation flash before the app went back to the home screen?
questions.why: Some apps, like Cash App, do not leave a static confirmation screen; they show a brief success animation (like a checkmark) and immediately return to the home screen, making it the only immediate proof of success.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to witness the brief visual confirmation of success, forcing them to manually dig through their transaction history to verify the payment went through if the agent misses it.
questions.check: Does the app show a brief success animation and then return to the home screen, with no static confirmation left on screen?
questions.say_example: A success checkmark flashed and then it returned to the home screen

questions.question: Do the amount and recipient match across the balance screen, the review screen, and the final confirmation?
questions.why: Verifying the recipient, amount, and privacy settings on the review screen against your starting balance ensures the math is correct before you pass the no-undo moment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally audit the transaction across its different stages to ensure your account balance reflects the exact payment made.
questions.check: Do the recipient, amount, and privacy setting on the review screen match what appears on the starting balance screen and the final confirmation?
questions.say_example: The review screen showed <$16>, but the confirmation shows <$24>

questions.question: Where do you go to view your payment history?
questions.why: Opening the settings menu from the chats tab is necessary to access your payment logs and verify the transaction.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose direct visibility into your account settings and the peace of mind of independently verifying the payment log yourself.
questions.check: Does reaching transaction history require opening the settings menu from the chats tab?
questions.say_example: Opened settings from chats to reach payment history

questions.question: Which transaction's details do you want to view?
questions.why: The screen shows the chats tab with a recent payment snippet of '₹1.00 · Testing', and selecting the correct thread allows you to verify the final transaction details.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally review the final payment record in your chat history to ensure the transaction was completed correctly.
questions.check: Does the chats tab show more than one payment-related thread to choose from?
questions.say_example: Opened the thread with <the payment snippet>

questions.question: No confirmation appeared on screen - does the Activity list actually show the payment as sent?
questions.why: Since the confirmation was not immediately displayed on screen, you must navigate to the Activity tab to verify the transaction.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the direct reassurance of seeing the final transaction record with your own eyes to guarantee the money was sent.
questions.check: Does the Activity list show this payment as sent, even though no confirmation screen appeared?
questions.say_example: No confirmation showed on screen, but Activity lists it as <sent/pending>

questions.question: Does this show as completed, with a transaction ID you can share?
questions.why: Verifying the completed status and capturing the transaction ID ensures the payment was successful and provides proof to share with the recipient.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the immediate reassurance of seeing the completed status and the ability to personally copy the transaction ID for the recipient.
questions.check: Does the activity entry show the status as completed, along with a transaction ID?
questions.say_example: This is marked completed, with transaction ID <the reference the app shows>.

questions.question: Did this get held up, needing a separate approval by text or email?
questions.why: Large or unusual peer-to-peer payments often trigger automated bank holds, requiring you to respond to a text or email from your bank before the funds are actually released.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the awareness that the payment is paused and the opportunity to promptly clear the security hold, leaving the recipient waiting for funds you thought were sent.
questions.check: Did the transaction trigger a security hold requiring approval through a separate text or email from your bank?
questions.say_example: Your bank is holding this and wants a separate approval by <text/email>

questions.question: Is the payment status showing as 'Pending Review' rather than completed?
questions.why: Fraud algorithms sometimes hold payments for manual review, meaning the recipient will not get the money instantly as expected.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the awareness that your payment is delayed by the platform, preventing you from communicating the delay to the recipient.
questions.check: Does the payment status show "Pending Review" rather than completed?
questions.say_example: This is sitting at Pending Review, not completed yet

questions.question: Does your final account balance confirm that the payment was actually sent?
questions.why: The account balance remained at $0.00, proving that the $1.00 transaction drafted earlier was never actually submitted.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to verify that the funds actually left your account and the transaction was successfully completed.
questions.check: Does the account balance still match the pre-payment amount, meaning the payment never actually went through?
questions.say_example: Balance is still <$65>, unchanged. This payment may not have gone through.

questions.question: Has your balance already dropped by the payment amount, even if the history list hasn't updated yet?
questions.why: Verifying that the available balance dropped from $685.52 to $680.52 confirms the payment was processed, even though the recent transactions list doesn't show it yet.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the immediate reassurance of seeing your account balance decrease to confirm the transfer was successful before the transaction log updates.
questions.check: Has the available balance dropped by the payment amount, even if the transaction list hasn't updated yet?
questions.say_example: Balance dropped from <$300> to <$275>, so this went through even though the list hasn't caught up

questions.question: Do you need to refresh the screen to verify the updated account balance?
questions.why: The screen still displays the previous available balance of $680.52, so refreshing is necessary to confirm the transaction was processed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means losing the immediate reassurance of seeing your funds successfully update in real time.
questions.check: Does the balance shown still reflect the pre-payment amount until the screen is refreshed?
questions.say_example: Refreshed the screen to pick up the updated balance

questions.question: What confirmation will you get after sending the money?
questions.why: Knowing that Zelle sends confirmation emails to both parties provides peace of mind that the transaction completed successfully.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the immediate reassurance of checking your own inbox to verify the transaction went through and the recipient was notified.
questions.check: Does the app state that it sends confirmation emails to both sender and recipient?
questions.say_example: This sends a confirmation email to both of you

questions.question: Is the transfer complete, or does the recipient need to register first?
questions.why: This matters because the confirmation screen warns that the recipient is unregistered and your account will not be debited until they sign up.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the awareness that their payment is currently pending and requires the recipient to take action before the money actually moves.
questions.check: Does the confirmation warn that the recipient is unregistered and the account won't be debited until they sign up?
questions.say_example: <Name> hasn't signed up yet, so nothing's actually been taken from your account until they do

questions.question: Do you want to check what your recipient needs to do to claim the money?
questions.why: The email shows the recipient must click a button to claim the money within 24 hours before the payment expires.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to understand exactly what steps the recipient must take to access the funds.
questions.verify_form: Check whether anyone verified the claim side - the email gives your recipient 24 hours before the payment dies; if the agent skipped that, the send can quietly expire.
questions.check: Does the email to the recipient say they must click a link to claim the money within a stated time limit before it expires?
questions.say_example: Your recipient has <24 hours> to claim this before it expires

questions.question: Do you need to download a receipt or just verify the final transfer status?
questions.why: The screen shows the transfer is currently 'In review' and provides the final exchange rate along with options to download a statement or report an issue.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally verify the estimated delivery timeline and decide if you need to keep a downloaded record of the transaction.
questions.verify_form: Check whether a receipt got saved - the screen offered a download and the agent chose; with no file kept, this transfer's proof lives only inside the app.
questions.check: Does the screen offer to download a statement or receipt for this transfer?
questions.say_example: There's a receipt to download here. Keep it, because this kind of payment has no chargeback.
